*Proof.* Since $a_{n+1}=(a_{n-1}-1)(b_n+1)$,

**Identity 2:** For $m \geq 1$, $\displaystyle\frac{b_m}{a_{m+3}} = \frac{1}{a_{m+1}(a_{m+1}-1)}$.

*Proof.* We have $a_{m+3}=(a_{m+1}-1)(b_{m+2}+1)$ (valid for $m\geq 0$) and $b_{m+2}+1 = a_{m+1}\,b_m$ (from $b_{m+2}=a_{m+1}\,b_m - 1$, valid for $m\geq 1$). Substituting:
$$a_{m+3} = (a_{m+1}-1)\cdot a_{m+1}\cdot b_m, \qquad\text{so}\qquad \frac{b_m}{a_{m+3}} = \frac{b_m}{(a_{m+1}-1)\,a_{m+1}\,b_m} = \frac{1}{a_{m+1}(a_{m+1}-1)}. \quad\checkmark$$

$$\sum_{n=3}^{N}\frac{b_n}{a_{n+1}} \stackrel{\text{Id.1}}{=} \sum_{n=2}^{N-1}\frac{1}{a_n-1}-\sum_{n=4}^{N+1}\frac{1}{a_n},$$

$$\sum_{n=3}^{N}\frac{b_{n-2}}{a_{n+1}} \stackrel{\text{Id.2}}{=} \sum_{n=3}^{N}\frac{1}{a_{n-1}(a_{n-1}-1)} = \sum_{n=2}^{N-1}\!\left(\frac{1}{a_n-1}-\frac{1}{a_n}\right).$$

$$\sum_{n=3}^{\infty}\frac{b_n-b_{n-2}}{a_{n+1}} = \frac{1}{a_2}+\frac{1}{a_3}.$$
